text: The principal of these things is the mastery of one's temper, and that coolness of mind, and serenity of countenance, which hinders us from discovering by words, actions, or even looks, those passions or sentiments by which we are inwardly moved or agitated; and the discovery of which gives cooler and abler people such infinite advantages over us, not only in great business, but in all the most common occurrences of life.
author: Philip Stanhope, 4th Earl of Chesterfield
locator: Letter LXXI, to his son, London, May 22, Old Style 1749
